prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Waiting screen enhancements (wait_info) are helpful and consistently yield statistically significant gains.
Adding a pet preview screen before the adoption certificate (new_screen) is helpful and produced a large significant gain (+15.4%).
Copy adjustments (copy), layout changes (layout), sign-in reordering (reorder), tutorials (redesign), and progress hints (hint) showed no clear effect.
Predictions underestimated large wins, such as the pet preview screen (+3.0% predicted vs +15.4% measured).
Predictions were generally too high for changes that showed no clear effect.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, copy: -0.5% over 1 test(s)
- adoption, new_screen: +15.4% over 1 test(s)
- choose_path, hint: -2.2% over 1 test(s)
- choose_path, layout: -1.4% over 1 test(s)
- finish, redesign: -3.0% over 1 test(s)
- home, wait_info: +5.4% over 2 test(s)
- sign_in, copy: +0.4% over 1 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: +3.1% over 1 test(s)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 70.5%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 88.5%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 22.5%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [home, wait_info] Interactive Sound and Animation Showcase on Waiting Screen: Add interactive pet sound triggers and animation previews to the waiting screen while the companion is generating. (why: Waiting screen enhancements (wait_info) consistently yield statistically significant conversion gains, and the home waiting step currently takes a median of 201s.)
1: [adoption, new_screen] Pet Naming and Personality Quiz Screen: Insert a dedicated Pet Naming and Personality Quiz screen right after picking a friend to deepen emotional attachment before finalizing adoption. (why: Adding dedicated pre-adoption screens proved highly effective (+15.4% gain from Pet Preview Screen), and custom pet setup issues are common in support.)
2: [home, wait_info] Desktop Ready Notification Trigger on Waiting Screen: Add a desktop system notification trigger switch on the waiting screen so users get alerted when pet preparation completes. (why: The home waiting step takes a median of 201s (mean 2336s), leading to user drop-off while waiting for pet creation.)
3: [choose_path, new_screen] Pet Archetype Selector Screen: Insert a visual companion archetype showcase screen before path selection to help users visually compare desktop pet styles. (why: Choose path drops 23.8% of users with a high mean time of 514s; presenting visual choices upfront clarifies the decision.)
4: [finish, hint] Desktop Tray Shortcut Hint on Home Intro: Add hotkey and tray icon instructions in the bottom hint bar of the home intro screen. (why: Multiple support emails mention confusion over how to access, hide, or control their pet once setup is finished.)
5: [finish, new_screen] Desktop Launcher Quick-Start Confirmation Screen: Insert a new quick-launch test screen at the end of onboarding where users verify their pet renders on the desktop before exiting. (why: The finish step has a low conversion rate of 64.8%, and 3 support emails reported the pet failing to show up on the desktop.)

scores.note: Waiting screen enhancements consistently yield significant gains, though home step drop-off is relatively low.
Adoption has a high drop-off rate (29.5%), support mentions setup issues, and new_screen changes show strong historical gains.
Addresses long waiting duration (mean 2336s) using proven wait_info pattern.
Choose_path drops 23.8% of users with long duration; new_screen format historically performs very well.
Target step loses 35.2% and support emails exist, but hint changes have shown no clear positive effect.
Target step has the highest drop-off (35.2%), supported by multiple emails and backed by high-confidence new_screen type.
